Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final innings. The crowd cheered loudly for Alyssa Healy as she walked off the field for the last time. While some fans hoped she would open the batting in her final game, the usual pair of Georgia Voll and Phoebe Litchfield comes out instead to score the final 25 runs. Kashvee Gautam will start with the ball for India Women. Let's go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

An easy chase for the Aussies - While the rest of the team collapsed, Pratika Rawal was the only Indian batter who fought hard against the tough conditions. She built a fighting partnership with Sneh Rana to push India past Australia's 125-run lead, but once Rana got out, the rest of the wickets fell quickly. Now, Australia needs just 25 runs to win, making the chase a mere formality.

The Aussies were brilliant with the ball again - The Australian bowlers were completely in control and kept the pressure on the hosts. Debutant Lucy Hamilton had a dream match, taking three crucial wickets to tear through the Indian batting lineup. She was fully supported by the rest of the attack, with Annabel Sutherland, Alana King, and Ashleigh Gardner all taking key wickets to stop India from getting back into the game.

It was a terrible start for India! India's second innings started disastrously under the tricky twilight conditions with the pink ball. The openers lost their wickets within the first two overs, and the middle order failed to build any strong partnerships. Despite some effort from players like Jemimah Rodrigues and captain Harmanpreet Kaur, the team was eventually bowled out for just 149, giving them a tiny lead of only 24 runs.

OUT! TAKEN! Ashleigh Gardner gets her second wicket and wraps things up. This is a short-length delivery, pitching just outside leg. Pratika Rawal opens her stance to pull it away over sqaure leg, but fails to time the shot well. The ball loops toward the left of the short fine leg region, where Annabel Sutherland takes an excellent diving catch. So, Australia just need 25 runs to win this one-off test.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going on this Moving Day. Pratika Rawal is just seven runs away from her maiden half-century, and she is marching alongside Sneh Rana toward the middle of the park. The players of Australia have scattered to take their fielding positions. It's Alana King who will kickstart proceedings with the ball. Rana to face the first ball of the day. Justin Langer expects the wicket to get better to bat on as the day goes on. Here we go!

Can India still fight? As we begin today's play, all Indian hopes rest on the shoulders of debutant Pratika Rawal. She has been the lone warrior so far, fighting bravely for her unbeaten 43, and has found steady support from Sneh Rana. This pair must bat out of their skins to erase the remaining deficit and give Australia a target to chase. Can India stage a miraculous comeback, or will Australia wrap things up quickly? Let's find out!

It was a shaky Indian reply - India's attempt to fight back in the second innings did not go to plan. Darcie Brown set the tone early by knocking over Smriti Mandhana, and the Australian bowlers never let off the pressure. Debutant Lucy Hamilton was the star with the ball, picking up three crucial wickets to leave the Indian batting lineup in tatters, with key players like Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh.

Australia on top! Yesterday was all about the Australian batters asserting their dominance. Annabel Sutherland continued her spectacular form with a magnificent 129. Alongside her, Ellyse Perry played a beautiful knock of 76, making history by becoming Australia's leading run-scorer in Women's Tests. Despite a fantastic four-wicket haul from India's debutant Sayali Satghare, Australia posted 323 to secure a massive 125-run lead.

Welcome to Day 3 - A very warm welcome to the third day of this solitary Test match! As things stand, Australia is firmly in the driver's seat. India ended Day 2 struggling at 105/6 in their second innings, still trailing by 20 runs. They have a mountain to climb today if they want to stay alive in this game.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Australia closing in - Take nothing away from the probing lines and lengths Australia bowled, but it was not as if the ball was doing corners and batting was impossible. Pratika Rawal showed the way with her discipline and, together with Sneh Rana, ensured there was no further damage before stumps. India still trail by 20 runs. Batting conditions should be a touch easier when play resumes on Day 3, but as we saw in the first session on Day 2, there was still enough in the surface for the quicks to exploit. Can India show the stomach for a fight? In all likelihood, Sunday, 8th March, will mark the final day of international cricket for Alyssa Healy. Play on Day 3 will begin at 10.50 am IST (5.20 am GMT). We look forward to having your company then. Cheers!

India falter under lights - Facing the pink ball under lights was always going to be a challenge, just as Australia had experienced on the opening day, but India did not help their cause with some questionable shot selection. After the openers fell early, Jemimah Rodrigues and Pratika Rawal stitched together a brief recovery before Rodrigues threw it away while attempting the scoop. Harmanpreet Kaur and Richa Ghosh also left much to be desired with their shot selection.

Perry's exit sparked India - The way the partnership was flourishing, it all looked ominous for the tourists, but Perry's departure injected life into the Indian effort on a scorching day. Beth Mooney was dropped on 0 but could not make the most of that lifeline, while Sutherland continued on her merry way even as wickets fell around her, with India chipping away through the second session. Into the tail, India hoped to keep the lead under 100, but Alana King and Lucy Hamilton added some valuable runs late on to push Australia's lead past that mark. By the end, the home side had stretched their advantage to 125.

Sutherland shone as Perry made history - Australia began the day with a 102-run deficit but were given a positive start by Ellyse Perry and Annabel Sutherland, as India were made to pay for their inconsistency with the ball. Sutherland went on to complete her third successive Test century and the fourth of her career, the most for any Australian women's batter in Tests. Perry too entered the record books, going past Karen Rolton to become Australia's leading Test scorer.

Australia in complete control - 118 runs, 31.4 overs and 8 wickets in the session. In Alyssa Healy's final international appearance, Australia have put on a dominant display. While the hosts did not quite bat the visitors out of the game with their first-innings effort, they came out firing with the ball and made the most of the conditions under lights. India have let themselves down with the bat and are now staring down the barrel.
